questions.question: Which part of smeltr reads from sources and delivers to destinations?
choices: A worker
The leader
A pipeline
A route
questions.answer: The leader holds the configuration, and workers move the data.

questions.question: The leader goes down. What happens to the data your workers are moving?
choices: It keeps flowing
It stops until the leader comes back
The workers hold it until the leader comes back
The workers send it to their destinations without the pipeline
questions.answer: It keeps flowing. Each worker runs the commit it already has.

questions.question: Where do you find the password for your first sign-in?
choices: In compose.yaml
In the leader's logs, from its first start
It's admin, until you change it
On the leader's sign-in page
questions.answer: In the leader's logs, from its first start. smeltr prints it once, and Docker keeps it there.

questions.question: The leader signed its own certificate. Why does the new worker trust it?
choices: It trusts whichever certificate it sees first
It doesn't check certificates inside Docker
Its enrollment code names the leader's certificate authority
You copy the certificate into the worker's system trust store
questions.answer: Its enrollment code names the leader's certificate authority, and the worker accepts only that one.

questions.question: Syslog carries no password. How does a Syslog receiver decide who may send to it?
choices: By the host name in each line
By the addresses you allow
By the program name in each line
It accepts every sender, and the pipeline drops the rest
questions.answer: By the addresses you allow.

questions.question: Why capture a sample before you build the pipeline?
choices: Workers deploy only pipelines that have a sample
Capturing opens the receiver's port
So you build and check the pipeline on lines that really arrive
The sample holds lines back until the pipeline is deployed
questions.answer: So the pipeline is built and checked against the lines that really arrive.

questions.question: Your pipeline parses each line into fields. Why keep event.original?
choices: It holds what went wrong when a line can't be read
It's the original line, the evidence of what really arrived
The pipeline reads its fields from it at the destination
The record can't be sent without it
questions.answer: It's the original line, the evidence of what really arrived.

questions.question: A Parser step has two patterns, and a line matches both. Which one is used?
choices: The one that reads the most fields
The last one in the list
Both, and their fields are merged
The first one in the list
questions.answer: The first one in the list.

questions.question: Why does it matter that the time is a datetime, not text?
choices: So smeltr sorts the records by time
So smeltr reads it into one standard form
So smeltr drops lines older than a day
So the line keeps its original text
questions.answer: A datetime has one standard form, ISO 8601, with the year and time zone the line left out filled in.

questions.question: Where does the Elasticsearch API key live, and why not in the configuration?
choices: In a secret on the leader, because the configuration is in Git
In the destination's settings, saved in Git with the rest of the configuration
On each worker, in a file you copy there
In the leader's logs, next to the first password
questions.answer: In a secret on the leader. The configuration is in Git, and secrets never go there.

questions.question: A deploy goes wrong. How do you undo it?
choices: Delete the branch it came from
Restart the workers
Roll back to the commit before it, in History
Change it back on the branch and save; the workers pick it up
questions.answer: Roll back to the commit before it, in History. The workers move back to that commit, and stay there until you release it.

questions.question: In the course's login feed, how do rows in and rows out compare?
choices: They're the same: every row in goes out
Fewer go out, because the pipeline drops the noise
Fewer go out, because the pipeline drops failed logins
More go out, one for each field
questions.answer: Fewer go out, because the pipeline drops the noise. Every login goes on to search.

questions.question: Where does smeltr list what needs your attention?
choices: On History
On Branches
In the worker's logs
On Issues
questions.answer: On Issues. A red banner on every page shows when there are any.

questions.question: A line doesn't match any pattern. By default, where does the record go?
choices: It's dropped
It waits on the worker until you fix the pattern
On to its destination, with what went wrong in smeltr.exception
Back to the sender, which sends it again
questions.answer: On to its destination, with what went wrong in smeltr.exception, and the line as it arrived in event.original.

questions.question: You changed a pattern. How do you know the old lines still read the same?
choices: The test you saved runs on the sample, and still passes
Nothing needed: a pattern change never alters how old lines read
A reviewer reads the new pattern
smeltr refuses a pattern that changes how old lines read
questions.answer: The test you saved runs on the sample, and still passes.

questions.question: Elasticsearch was down. Why was no login lost?
choices: smeltr sent the records to another destination
smeltr wrote them to a file for you to send again
The worker passed them to the leader
smeltr held the records and tried again until Elasticsearch came back
questions.answer: smeltr held the records and tried again until Elasticsearch came back. In a longer outage, rsyslog's queue holds the rest.

questions.question: What does a pipeline do, and what joins it to a source and its destinations?
choices: It reads from a source; a worker group joins it
It shapes each record with a list of steps; a route joins it
It stores records; a branch joins it
It's a group of workers; the leader joins it
questions.answer: A pipeline is a list of steps that shapes each record. A route joins it to one source and its destinations.

questions.question: You saved a change on a branch. Why don't your workers run it?
choices: Workers pick up a branch only after a restart
Workers run main, which changes only when a change is reviewed and deployed
A branch needs a new sample before it runs
A branch runs only on the leader's own worker
questions.answer: Workers run main. Main changes only when a change is reviewed and deployed.

questions.question: A new worker must join your fleet. What does it need from the leader?
choices: The administrator's password
A copy of the configuration repository
An enrollment code, minted for its group
A certificate from a public certificate authority
questions.answer: An enrollment code, minted for its group.

questions.question: Why use TCP rather than UDP for syslog, wherever the sender can send it?
choices: TCP encrypts the lines
UDP can't carry a line longer than 100 bytes
smeltr receives syslog only over TCP
Over UDP, a busy receiver drops what it can't take
questions.answer: Over UDP nothing tells the sender to slow down, so a busy receiver drops what it can't take.

questions.question: A field you need is wrong in Elasticsearch. How do you find which step changed it?
choices: Open the pipeline on a sample, and pause the records after each step
Read the worker's logs
Remove one step at a time, and deploy after each
Look at the field on History
questions.answer: Open the pipeline on a sample, and pause the records after each step to see them as they leave it.

questions.question: Your pipeline can't read a line. How do you find out?
choices: The worker stops the route and raises an issue
The receiver refuses the line, and the sender's log shows it
The record carries it in smeltr.exception, and Map counts exceptions on each step
The worker's logs list each line it can't read
questions.answer: The record carries it, in smeltr.exception. On Map, the pipeline's Steps tab counts exceptions on each step.

questions.question: You want each record to name the program that wrote it, as process.name, and to deploy that. In what order do you work?
choices: Rename it on main, check it on the sample, lock the new test, and save
Start a branch, rename it, deploy from the branch, then check it on the sample
Start a branch, rename it, check it on the sample, lock the new test, review and deploy
Start a branch, rename it, deploy it, then check it on the sample and review
questions.answer: Work on a branch, so the workers keep running main. Rename program to process.name, check it on the sample, and lock the new result as the test. Then open it for review, approve and deploy it.
